expected.summary: sch2pdf writes the saved schematic to {dir}/Demo.pdf; verified by the file, pages listed.

rows.reason: schematic export always writes one PDF of every sheet; there is no call with nothing to write.

expected.summary: --output must name a .pdf file; refused at the preview.
The session has no such project open.

A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents. (Run the matrix with --mode session.)

An earlier export to the same file was interrupted: its CLI process was ended (Task Manager) while sch2pdf ran, so its outcome is unknown and the PDF's target stays locked until operation resolve: E_CONFLICT target_locked.
Run under a scope file that does not cover the target ({dir}/Demo.pdf); nothing is previewed to the application's files or sent.

While a schematic create job of this tool is still drawing in Designer, the session reports busy. Only --session is given: a busy Designer may not say which project it has open, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Designer before the call, such as Setup > Settings or Help > About. The session is reported blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a blocked Designer may not say which project it has open. The runtime refuses on the session state, although sch2pdf itself would not need Designer.

rows.reason: schematic export runs the headless sch2pdf on the project files and never calls Designer during the write, so there is no connection to lose; an instance that stops answering before the call is the busy row, and an sch2pdf that fails is E_NATIVE_FAILURE.

expected.summary: Designer holds unsaved changes (schematic create not yet saved): the PDF shows the project as last saved, and the preview's action and the result's warnings say so.
The call waits before its read-back, and meanwhile the new PDF is deleted (--tamper): the check of the file finds it missing.
